text:
emma (oncall): Paging: increased 5xx rate for inference cluster in az1a, started seeing evictions and attach failures. alerts: infer-500-rate > 5% for 10m.
pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-4452 - az1a ephemeral capacity surge / inference errors. Severity: sev2.
omar: I can see a cluster spike on az1a g5 pool, host-level OOM evictions + ENI attach errors. CPU and net tx drops correlate.
lee: Network graphs show tx_queue_depth rising around 20:03 UTC, packet retransmits up ~12x.
katie: Is this just one AZ? Any cross-AZ impact?
omar: So far only az1a. Cross-region fallback traffic is healthy. We are seeing autoscaler failing to start new pods in az1a due to ENI attach throttling (AWS attach rate limit).
emma (oncall): Customer impact: a subset of real-time infer requests are returning 502/504 or timing out; async batch jobs queueing. CS flagged two customers reporting latency spikes (customer-a, customer-b). ETA on mitigation?
raj: Steps: 1) Pause low-priority background embeddings and reroute to eu1 fallback. 2) Enable model-fallback to quantized-4bit variant for latency-sensitive routes in az1a routing policy. 3) Increase cross-AZ steering weight by 30%.
infra-bot: Executing step 1: /runapi scale service embeddings-backfill --region az1a --min-instances 0 --reason "incident PD-4452"
lee: Confirmed embeddings-backfill scaled to 0 in az1a.
omar: Starting canary reroute: adjusting traffic-split config on router: 
```
route config set inference-default {
  az_weights: { az1a: 60, eu1a: 30, usw2a: 10 }
  fallback_policy: prefer-cross-region
}
```
katie: Suggest we also throttle per-tenant QPS for non-edu/tier1 customers to preserve capacity. Can we push a quick token-based limit?
emma (oncall): Doing manual rate-limit: /admin throttle set --scope nonpaid --qps 0.5 --region az1a
infra-bot: Rate limit applied.
raj: Also enabling model-fallback: set model_priority for inference-default: [redwood-llama-13b-4bit, redwood-llama-13b, redwood-7b]. This will serve smaller quantized model when larger fails to load.
omar: Noted several host-level errors pointing to nic reset + ENI attach failures in system logs: 
```
kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.1 enp0s...: TX hung - resetting
aws: ENI attach rate limit exceeded for account
```
lee: Reached out to AWS support with packet captures and ENI errors, ticket #AWSSUPPORT-123456. They acknowledged a regional control plane delay.
customer-success: Heads up, escalating to vendor contacts for impacted customers. Drafting customer message: "We're aware of elevated errors in az1a; we've routed traffic and applied mitigations. Next update in 30m."
emma (oncall): Monitoring: error rate dropped from 7.2% to 2.1% after reroute and rate-limits. Latency p50 for inference routes down ~160ms. Still seeing intermittent evictions.
raj: If we continue to see ENI attach failures, plan B: move affected pools to dedicated reserved capacity in other AZs and failover models. That requires coordination with Alloc team.
omar: Quick temp fix: disable instance scale-up in az1a to avoid triggering additional attach requests. Set autoscaler max to current.
infra-bot: Autoscaler config updated: max_replicas locked at 240 for az1a.
lee: Observability note: KV cache miss rate climbed when traffic moved cross-region, causing small spike in end-to-end latency. We're warming caches proactively.
emma (oncall): Handoff plan: primary oncall remains until 23:00 UTC, then hand off to night team (lee). Leave pager duty escalation for PD-4452 active.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff scheduled: 23:00 UTC -> lee (night-oncall).
katie: Postmortem notes start: suspected root cause: AWS ENI attach throttling triggered by transient control-plane issue causing instance net resets and subsequent evictions. Secondary: autoscaler reaction increased attach attempts.
omar: Action items: - formalize autoscaler backoff to avoid attach storms - add ENI attach metrics and alert for attach-rates approaching provider limits - update runbook for cross-AZ rapid-steer.
customer-success: Sending interim update to impacted customers now.
emma (oncall): Closing loop: metrics are stable but not fully recovered; leaving incident open until AWS confirms region control-plane healthy. Next update 22:45 UTC. :white_check_mark:
